about.title: Maricopa Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Maricopa is a small place—roughly 1,200 people in Kern County, gathered along California Street and Route 166, where most folks know each other by name. When someone here dies because another person or business was careless, the loss ripples through the whole town. Public records for 2018, the most recent finalized year, list no traffic deaths and no injury collisions inside city limits. Those numbers are a comfort, but they don't cover every fatal event a family might face: a crash farther out on Rt 166, a workplace accident, a medical error, or an unsafe property. Under California law, a wrongful death case is a civil claim brought first by a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, then by certain dependents or heirs. It runs separately from any criminal charges. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. LawProactive connects Maricopa families with an independent attorney, at no cost, so you can ask questions before deciding anything.

whyChoose.title: Why Maricopa Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can sort out where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock matters
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting connected early protects your right to act.

items.title: Every kind of loss counts
items.desc: Recoverable damages go beyond funeral and burial costs to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency—no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Public records show zero traffic deaths in Maricopa for 2018. Does that mean a wrongful death claim isn't realistic here?
items.answer: Not at all. Those figures only count collisions inside city limits for one reporting year, and many Maricopa residents travel Rt 166 and beyond every day. Wrongful death claims also arise from workplace accidents, medical negligence, and unsafe properties, none of which appear in traffic statistics. What matters is whether someone else's carelessness caused the death, wherever it happened.

items.question: The driver who caused the crash is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that proceeds separately from any criminal prosecution, and it can move forward whether or not charges are filed or result in a conviction. The two cases have different goals: one seeks punishment, the other seeks compensation for your family's losses. An attorney can explain how the timing of each might affect the other.

items.question: How long do we have to bring a wrongful death case in Kern County?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file. If a city, county, or state agency may be responsible—for example, a poorly maintained public roadway—a claim must first be presented to that entity on a much shorter timeline. Because these deadlines are firm, it helps to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later, even if you are not ready to decide.
